maps.summary:
I surveyed the repo for everything that bears on giving each agent its own browser. Nothing for a browser is built yet. Three findings matter most.

(1) A browser in today's sandbox could not reach the web. ACS sandboxes are created with internet access off. The only allowed destination is the model gateway's IP. There is no NAT. The egress gateway/proxy (WBS 2.7) is planned but not built.

(2) The pieces needed to add a browser as a platform tool already exist. The `PlatformTools` trait and ToolSet are there, and MCP content arrays can carry images. The `computer_*` pattern (risk tiers, timeouts, a wait state) can be copied. The design docs already say that if a "cloud browser" is ever bought from AgentBay, it should be called by the server as a platform tool, not run inside the sandbox.

(3) Nothing lets the user watch or take over the agent's browser. The app-facing gateway never talks to sandboxes. The event log cuts long strings at 16 KiB, so screenshots cannot ride the event stream. `SandboxProvider` has no "expose a port" call.

Correction to the product context: the desktop does NOT use chromiumoxide. chromiumoxide is only planned (WBS 14.4). The Mac tools are generic screen control (ScreenCaptureKit/CGEvent/NSWorkspace), and `computer_open` simply opens a URL in the user's default browser. They are macOS-only and have never been run on a real Mac.

Sizing and storage today:
- Sandboxes are 1 vCPU with 1–2 GiB RAM (per manifest). The image has no Chromium and no CJK fonts. OpenClaw's image does ship playwright-core, but not a browser binary.
- `InstanceLimits` is only model-gateway rate limits, not CPU or memory.
- Agent HOME is `workspace/.thinktin/home`. A browser profile there would survive, because on ACS the workspace is tar'd, encrypted with the user's DEK and stored in OSS. `/sandbox/home`, `/tmp` and sockets are not saved. Archives are capped at 4 GiB.
- Approvals use ACP tool kinds that the agent reports itself (`fetch`, `execute`, …). These express user intent only; they are not a security boundary.
- Platform tools today reach only Claude, Codex and Hermes, not Pi or OpenClaw. Claude and Codex ask for approval before every MCP call.

AgentBay was already researched on 2026-10-28 and rejected as the sandbox (reasons below). It is noted as a possible future "cloud browser" platform tool.

facts.claim: Sandbox image base is node:24-trixie-slim; agent-shim compiled from source
Image installs only bash ca-certificates curl git jq less procps python3 python3-venv ripgrep unzip xz-utils; no browser, no Xvfb/VNC, no fonts, no compiler
Processes run as non-root 'user' (uid 1001); image HOME=/sandbox/home, workdir /sandbox/workspace
envd (port 49983) is required but not yet in the image; source still to be decided
Current template sizes: Pi 508 MB, Hermes 587 MB, Claude 695 MB, Codex 852 MB, OpenClaw 905 MB
OpenClaw's image contains playwright-core 1.63.0 (a dependency, licence notices tracked), but no browser binary is installed
agent-shim sets NO_BROWSER=1 for Codex
Per-agent sandbox size comes from the manifest [runtime]: Claude 1 vCPU/2048 MB, Codex 1/1024, Hermes 1/2048, OpenClaw 1/2048, Pi 1/1024
The manifest allows 1-16 vCPU and 256-65536 MB, so a browser-capable agent can be sized up per template
The control plane builds CreateSpec from manifest vcpu/memory and config disk_mb; default Resources is 1 core / 1 GiB / 5 GiB disk
InstanceLimits is only model-gateway rate limiting (120 requests/min, 8 concurrent), not CPU or memory
On ACS, CPU and memory come from the per-template SandboxSet sized from the manifest [runtime]; the create body does not carry resources
The test SandboxSet pod spec is 1 CPU / 1Gi memory / 30Gi ephemeral storage; the preheat-pool image is Alibaba's code-interpreter:v1.6
Pricing assumptions for overseas sandboxes: ¥0.123 per core-hour and ¥0.062 per GB-hour; about ¥16-18 per active user per month; paused sandboxes billed for storage only
A 1-core 2G sandbox costs about ¥0.25/hour; the traffic-proxy sidecar may round the size up; paused sandboxes still pay for 30 GiB ephemeral storage, about ¥36/month
The ACS controller adds a per-sandbox traffic proxy of 0.2 core / 128M; sandbox-gateway streamIdleTimeout defaults to 600 s
Architecture cost table: the platform pays for egress traffic ('网页浏览、文件下载', i.e. web browsing and file downloads), rate-limited per instance; anti-abuse caps on CPU time and egress
Sandbox egress default: deny all and allow only the listed targets (usually just the model gateway)
ACS create sets allow_internet_access=false plus network.allowOut; allowOut takes IP/CIDR/domain only, with no wildcard and no port
The Tokyo config allows only the service machine IP (model gateway on 8790); the security group opens only 8790 to the VPC
ACS sandboxes have no NAT and do not reach the internet; adding NAT/ALB is avoided for cost
The egress gateway and network policy (WBS 2.7, P1) are not built; the threat model lists the egress allowlist and metadata block as the top pre-launch todo
Planned design: filter egress through an egress gateway by policy; credentials injected by the egress proxy; policy configurable per template
All five agents work offline; the egress policy can be 'deny by default, allow only the model gateway'
llm-gw already has an SSRF guard (https only, public-IP-only resolver, no redirects) and an optional --egress-proxy

The control plane reaches a sandbox only through envd on port 49983. The three route styles all put the port in the URL: Host header '49983-<id>.<domain>', wildcard DNS, or Kruise path '<base>/kruise/<id>/49983/<path>'
The SandboxProvider trait has create/get/exec/pause/resume/snapshot/destroy/file I/O only, with no method to expose or proxy another port
Cube templates are registered with --expose-port 49983; Cube data plane uses allowPublicTraffic false plus traffic tokens
Each ACS sandbox is a Pod with its own IP; sandbox tokens are bound to the Pod IP that the model gateway sees
In-cluster traffic (sandbox-manager, envd, model gateway) is plaintext HTTP; how the service machine reaches sandbox-manager is still undecided (internal SLB or move into the cluster)
The app-facing gateway routes never touch sandboxes: grep for 'sandbox' in gateway routes returns nothing
The shim runs with --home .thinktin/home and cwd = workspace, so agent HOME = /sandbox/workspace/.thinktin/home and agent state persists with the workspace
ACS has no volume. Before destroying a sandbox the control plane tars the workspace and encrypts it per user DEK (1 MiB chunks, AES-256-GCM) into OSS, then restores it on rebuild
Only the workspace is archived: /sandbox/home and paths outside the workspace are not saved; tar skips sockets; files changing during packing may be partial
Archive cap is 4 GiB by default (larger ones are not archived and stay paused); account deletion drops the DEK (crypto-shred)
Lifecycle defaults: idle pause after 10 minutes, archive after 7 days. Tokyo config archives after 1 hour and does not pause while waiting for approval
Per-user encryption of Cube volumes is not done yet (it depends on Cube storage)
Platform tools implement PlatformTools { tools(), call(ctx, name, args) -> ToolOutput }; ToolOutput.content is an MCP content array (can carry images)
ToolSet merges providers and dispatches by name
The shim injects platform tools as an MCP server named 'thinktin' via agent-shim mcp-bridge over a Unix socket
Platform tools reach only Claude, Codex and Hermes; Pi and OpenClaw are not supported yet. Claude and Codex ask for approval before each MCP tool call; Hermes does not
The executor builds each run's tool list. It adds computer_* only if the user has a computer, then filters everything by the run grant's platform_tools
Default grant includes all platform tool groups plus computer_* names
computer_* calls run in a separate task. If the computer is offline the run goes to WaitingDevice and resumes when it reconnects
Side-effect platform tools are executed once per run (idempotency cache); computer tools are not in that list

The computer tool catalog has three risk tiers: read-only (list_dir, read_file, screenshot), normal (write_file, open URL/app/file, click, type, key), high (delete, run; phone signature every time). Timeouts are 60 s and 15 min
Routing goes run -> instance -> user -> the user's online computer, never taken from agent output. Results are polled every 2 s with DB notify
The relay is an outbound wss from the Mac and accepts only macOS devices. Size limits: 16 MiB frame, 4 MiB args, 12 MiB result
The desktop opens https URLs with any valid capability token; click/type/key need a token covering the frontmost app
Mac tools are ScreenCaptureKit screenshot (JPEG, long edge up to 1568 px), CGEvent mouse/keys and NSWorkspace open. There is no DOM/CDP browser control
The desktop crate has no chromiumoxide/enigo/xcap dependency; chromiumoxide is only planned in WBS 14.4 and the architecture stack
The Mac App code is written but has never been run on a Mac
Windows desktop is not planned yet
Screenshot results are returned as MCP image content blocks
App event stream is a WebSocket of stored JSON events (seq/kind/payload) with resume
Run-log events truncate any string over 16 KiB and replace payloads over 256 KiB with a stub; a run's log is capped at 64 MiB, so base64 screenshots cannot be shown through events
Platform tool results go back to the shim as commands; the executor does not log them as events
Artifacts are downloaded as attachments (HTML is not rendered), which is a possible path for saved screenshots
No live-view, remote-desktop or takeover feature is designed anywhere: a docs grep for 画面/接管/VNC/云浏览器 finds only the AgentBay note
The Mac menubar shows the current tool via DesktopObserver.on_activity ('being controlled')
Pre-authorization uses ACP tool kinds (read, edit, delete, move, search, execute, think, fetch, switch_mode, other). Kinds are reported by the agent itself and are not a security boundary
PlanPolicy.preauthorized_tools is empty by default; approval timeout is 24 h; the shim runs with --on-unlisted ask
Example pre-auth scope '可以搜索网页' ('may search the web'); high-risk computer actions can never be pre-authorized
Web content is treated as untrusted (prompt-injection source)
Vault: the agent knows only names; thinktin-vault injects values into env/stdin/args. Exfiltration of revealed values depends on the 2.7 allowlist

AgentBay was researched 2026-10-28 and not used. Reasons: unavailable in Tokyo (domestic account is mainland-only; Singapore needs an international account); Linux sandbox egress cannot be locked (domain whitelist is Windows-only; *.aliyuncs.com always allowed); custom image needs Pro at ¥999/month with a 2c4G minimum; max run 1000 min and 72 h hibernation; no stdin and not E2B, so a new backend would take about 1.5-3 weeks

The AgentBay note suggests that for a future cloud browser / cloud PC, the Tokyo server calls AgentBay as an agent platform tool outside the sandbox layer, preferring an international Singapore account
AgentBay pricing noted: Basic tier free with 10 concurrent; CPU ¥0.12 per core-hour, memory ¥0.05 per GB-hour, billed per second; about 200 free hours for new users
The user decided on 10-28: launch for 10 test users, cheapest first; AgentBay not used this time
The early discussion proposed FC AgentRun hosted sandboxes (built-in code interpreter and browser) for launch
The FC/Agent sandbox 极速版 (express edition) E2B API supports port access; pause needs whitelisting; kept only as a fallback

implications: Build-it-ourselves (browser inside each sandbox) first needs WBS 2.7. Today a browser there could reach only the model gateway IP. The open web needs either NAT (cost, and it breaks the 'no internet' baseline) or a filtering egress proxy on the service machine plus another security-group port. That proxy must also block internal IPs and metadata, cap bandwidth and log traffic. This is the largest piece of work and is security-critical, because browsing pulls prompt-injection content into an agent that holds vault values and cookies.
ACS allowOut takes no wildcards or ports, so a domain allowlist for a general browser is impractical at the ACS layer. The policy has to live in our own proxy (CONNECT/SNI allowlist or denylist).

Sandboxes are sized at 1 vCPU / 1-2 GiB. Chromium plus an agent will likely need about 2-4 GiB (inference, not measured). Raising runtime.memory_mb in a manifest is a one-line change, but cost scales at about ¥0.062 per GB-hour on ACS. The image needs Chromium (or Playwright browsers) plus CJK fonts, adding several hundred MB to 0.5-0.9 GB templates.

Browser profiles and cookies placed under the agent HOME (workspace/.thinktin/home) would persist and be encrypted at rest in OSS archives. Profiles under /sandbox/home or /tmp would be lost on archive. Browser caches must be excluded or capped, or they will bloat archives toward the 4 GiB limit. Cookies are high-value secrets inside an untrusted sandbox.

Lifecycle pauses after 10 minutes idle and, in Tokyo, archives after 1 hour, so a running browser process will not survive. Only the on-disk profile does. Long-lived streams (CDP or VNC websockets) may hit the 600 s sandbox-gateway idle timeout.

A live view or user takeover needs new plumbing either way. Today the app cannot reach a sandbox, and screenshots cannot ride the event stream (16 KiB string cap). Options are: a new authenticated gateway endpoint that proxies a second sandbox port, which the envd route scheme hints is possible but is untested and not in the SandboxProvider trait; periodic screenshots stored as blobs or artifacts; or a vendor-hosted viewer URL (AgentBay-style).

The 'buy' path fits the existing architecture well. Add a BrowserTools PlatformTools provider (browser_open/snapshot/click/type...) that returns MCP image and text content, copying the computer_* pattern: risk tiers, timeouts, WaitingDevice-style waits, grant scoping. The browser then runs outside our sandbox, so sandbox egress stays locked to the model gateway. Caveats: only Claude, Codex and Hermes receive platform tools today; Claude and Codex prompt for approval on every MCP call unless that is pre-authorized; the AgentBay account and region mismatch (domestic account is mainland-only, Tokyo is unsupported) needs an international Singapore account or a cross-region call.

Reusing the user's own Mac browser (computer_open + screenshot + click) exists but is macOS-only, untested on real hardware, coordinate-based (no DOM) and depends on the user's computer being online. It suits 'act as me with my logins', not a per-agent browser.

The per-hour cost of AgentBay (¥0.12 per core-hour + ¥0.05 per GB-hour) is close to ACS (¥0.123 + ¥0.062). The decision therefore rests mainly on engineering effort, egress control, region and compliance, and live-view support, more than on unit price.
unknowns: Whether ACS sandbox-manager (v0.6.13) routes ports other than 49983 via /kruise/<id>/<port>/ (needed for CDP or noVNC); never tested on a real cluster
Actual RAM/CPU headroom inside 1-2 GiB sandboxes with Chromium running; not measured
Whether ACS pod ephemeral storage is encrypted at rest while running or paused; not documented in the repo
AgentBay browser-specific features (live view URL, CDP endpoint, session persistence, pricing of the browser image) are not recorded in the repo; only general sandbox findings are
Whether OpenClaw's built-in browser tooling (it ships playwright-core) is active or reachable; the shim config only sets tools.exec.mode=ask
Whether MCP platform-tool calls in Claude/Codex can be pre-authorized by ACP kind (they currently prompt per call)
Compliance and legal implications of browsing from a Tokyo IP on behalf of mainland users, or of routing to mainland AgentBay; not assessed in the docs
The real ACS cluster test checklist (egress blocked, metadata blocked, pause/resume, IP stability) is still pending (docs/sandbox-acs.md:114-125), so even the current network baseline is unverified

facts.claim: AgentBay offers four core environments: Browser Use (浏览器), Computer Use (云电脑, Windows or Linux), Code Space (代码空间) and Mobile Use (云手机, Android). Access is through SDK or MCP. The page says Browser Use is compatible with the Playwright/Puppeteer API style, supports headless and headed modes, and can load browser extensions. Page lastModifiedTime: 2026-05-20.
Official system images: linux_latest (default when image_id is omitted), windows_latest, browser_latest (cloud browser), code_latest, mobile_latest. Page modified 2026-03-13.

SDKs exist for Python (pip install wuying-agentbay-sdk), TypeScript (npm wuying-agentbay-sdk), Go (github.com/aliyun/wuying-agentbay-sdk/golang) and Java (Maven com.aliyun:agentbay-sdk). License is Apache-2.0. Auth is an API key from the AgentBay console, set as AGENTBAY_API_KEY.

Package versions: PyPI wuying-agentbay-sdk latest is 0.22.3 (uploaded 2026-06-04); the first PyPI release was 0.3.2 on 2025-06-25. npm wuying-agentbay-sdk latest is 0.22.0 (2026-06-03). The GitHub repo had a commit on 2026-10-28 and about 1.1k stars.

Browser flow: create a session with image_id='browser_latest', call session.browser.initialize(BrowserOption()), then get a CDP WebSocket URL with session.browser.get_endpoint_url() and attach with Playwright's chromium.connect_over_cdp(endpoint_url).

The official Browser Use page says get_endpoint_url (the CDP link) is not available on the Basic plan and needs a paid plan: '该方法不支持Basic权益包订阅使用，需先订阅高级权益后使用'. It also says you can open resource_url to watch the sandbox run. Page modified 2026-03-16.

The SDK docs call Session Link (get_link) 'an exclusive premium feature for paid subscription users (Pro/Ultra)'. Custom service ports are open by default only in the range 30100-30199. The example CDP URL format is wss://gw-cn-hangzhou-ai-linux.wuyinggw.com:8008/websocket_ai/{token}.
On GitHub issue #407 (Oct 17, 2025), a maintainer said 'The Session Link feature is currently in whitelist-only access' and that access requires applying by email.

Browser Context keeps cookies, cache, local storage, session storage, preferences and extensions across sessions (BrowserContext(context_id, auto_upload=True); delete the session with sync_context=True). It is supported only on browser_latest and linux_latest, not on windows_latest.
resource_url opens the cloud environment in any web browser 'with real-time video stream and full mouse/keyboard control'.

The MCP-returned sandbox link has a limited validity period and a limited number of opens ('该链接具有有效期限制和打开次数限制'). Keyboard and mouse interaction can be switched with &input=true&keyboard=true or through the Web SDK.

Call For User (BrowserOption(call_for_user=True)) sends messages such as code 101 'captcha request', 102 'login request' and 103 'pay request', each with action 'takeover' and max_wait_time 180s. The app opens session.resource_url for the human and then calls session.browser.send_takeover_done(id). Auto CAPTCHA solving sends pause/resume (codes 201/202, max wait 60s).

CAPTCHA solving is opt-in (BrowserOption(use_stealth=True, solve_captchas=True)). It 'only supports automatic resolution of slider-type CAPTCHAs'; text CAPTCHAs are listed as future work. Resolution 'typically completes within 30 seconds'.

Fingerprints can be random (device, OS, locale), synced from a local browser, constructed by hand, or persisted across sessions. Random works on all images. Local sync, construct and persistence work only on browser_latest and linux_latest.
The billing plan table lists 'device fingerprint' (设备指纹) as an Ultra-only advanced feature.

Proxy options: a custom HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy with optional authentication; the Wuying proxy service with a 'restricted' strategy (fixed IP for the session's lifetime) or a 'polling' strategy (rotating pool, pollsize); and a 'managed' proxy (your own pool managed by Wuying) with polling/sticky/rotating/matched strategies and country, province, city or ISP filters. Managed proxy requires contacting sales.

Image settings support 'network redirection' of the sandbox's traffic over SOCKS5 to a customer-supplied public IP, either for all traffic (global mode) or for listed domains only (whitelist mode). Other settings: maximum run time 1-1000 minutes, maximum hibernation 1-72 hours, idle release 1-1000 minutes, fixed or adaptive resolution up to 1920x1080. 'Normal network' allows at most 200 concurrent sessions on 5 Mbps shared bandwidth. 'Advanced network' allows at most 1000 concurrent sessions on dedicated, traffic-billed bandwidth (2-200 Mbps per session). System images 'support multiple regions and specs by default'. Page modified 2026-04-28.

International docs for custom image settings say a custom VPC 'must be in the China (Hangzhou) region. Only vSwitches in Hangzhou Zone B (cn-hangzhou-b) are supported'. The same page still contains '[To be verified in console]' placeholders. Updated: Aug 28.

Network (Beta) can redirect a cloud session's traffic out through the user's own local network: get a bind token, run ./rick-cli -m bind -t <token> locally, then create the session with beta_network_id. The stated purpose is to reduce site risk-control problems.

Session replay is recorded with rrweb (DOM changes, console output, network activity) when the session is created with enable_browser_replay=True. Replays are viewed in the console at agentbay.console.aliyun.com/session-log.
Screenshots: session.browser.operator.screenshot() returns base64, and session.browser.screenshot(page) returns bytes. Both support full-page capture and PNG or JPEG output.

File transfer between the caller and the sandbox uses session.file_system.upload_file() and download_file() (binary supported). The browser 'Upload/Download' section of the example index is empty. The browser example (file_upload_download.py) does not actually upload a file and only says 'actual file upload may require specific handling'. No documentation was found on where browser-initiated downloads are saved or how to retrieve them.
browser_latest runs Chromium only. Chrome can be chosen only on Computer Use images (linux_latest). windows_latest has no SDK browser automation, CDP or proxies.

MCP server: SSE at https://agentbay.wuying.aliyuncs.com/v2/sse?APIKEY=...&IMAGEID=browser_latest, Streamable HTTP at https://agentbay.wuying.aliyuncs.com/v2/mcp?APIKEY=...&IMAGEID=..., or stdio via npx -y wuying-agentbay-mcp-server. Page modified 2026-03-13.

LifecyclePolicy (SDK 0.20.0+): idle_release_timeout defaults to 5 minutes (backend minimum 3), max_runtime defaults to 30 minutes, and manual_release=True turns off auto-release. session.keep_alive() resets the idle timer. Released sessions cannot be recovered.

Console policy: release after MCP inactivity 1-1000 minutes, release after user inactivity 3-1000 minutes, maximum single run 1-1000 minutes. Trial accounts can auto-create at most 10 desktops. Page modified 2026-08-20.

SDK 0.22 regions: cn-hangzhou (default, agentbay.cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com), ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) and us-east-1 (Virginia). 'Domestic (China) API keys typically work with cn-hangzhou. International API keys typically work with ap-southeast-1 or us-east-1. API keys are region-specific and cannot be used across different unit regions.'

The help center (modified 2026-03-13) instead lists endpoints Shanghai (default, wuyingai.cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com) and Singapore (wuyingai.ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com). Using Singapore requires an API key created on the international site.
The international product page says 'Deployed in Singapore'. The domestic product page says '无影AgentBay 国际站已上线' and also says it relies on Alibaba Cloud's global distributed infrastructure.

Domestic pricing (CNY; billing page lastModifiedTime 2026-06-24):
- Basic: free, 10 concurrent sessions, 100 GiB storage.
- Pro: CNY 999/month, 200 concurrent sessions, 1 TiB storage, 50 custom images (5 enabled at once), GetLink.
- Ultra: CNY 1499/month, adds scale-out at CNY 10 per concurrent session per month, device fingerprint and priority access.
- Pay-as-you-go: CPU CNY 0.12/core/hour and memory CNY 0.05/GB/hour, both billed per second.
- Credits: CNY 0.05 each. The Browser Use Agent costs 16.8 Credits per million input tokens and 134.4 per million output tokens.
- Premium bandwidth: CNY 0.8/GB inbound, comes with an SLA.
- Storage over quota: CNY 0.0002/GiB/hour.
- Basic bandwidth: 10 Mbps, no SLA.
- GetLink requires enterprise real-name verification.

The domestic billing FAQ says idle sessions are billed: as long as a session is running and not deleted, its CPU and memory keep accruing charges. Pay-as-you-go cannot be paused; the only way to stop charges is to disable the API key.

The domestic billing example is internally inconsistent. The CPU line uses CNY 0.2/core/hour while the price table says CNY 0.12. The line items add up to CNY 16,676.104, but the stated total is CNY 18,676.104.

International pricing (USD; page 'Updated: Jun 25'):
- Plans: Pro USD 149/month, Ultra USD 225/month, scale-out USD 1.5 per concurrent session per month.
- Compute: CPU USD 0.027/core/hour, memory USD 0.0113/GB/hour, billed per second.
- Other items: Credits USD 0.0267 each, premium bandwidth USD 0.123/GB, storage USD 0.000045/GiB/hour.
- Concurrency and storage quotas are the same as domestic (10/200/200 sessions; 100 GiB/1 TiB storage).
- The international plan table does not list a GetLink row.

Domestic new-user trial: a one-time 100-point voucher (积分). Browser Use costs 0.5 points/hour, Code Space 0.5, Computer Use 1 and Mobile Use 1. Points cover compute only, not Credits, network or storage. Only real-name-verified main accounts qualify, not RAM users. Page modified 2026-05-18.
International trial: 100 points, Browser Use about 0.71 points/hour, Computer Use about 1.43 points/hour. Updated: Jun 02.
Billing changed on 2025-10-28 00:00 Beijing time: points packs stopped being sold, and plan subscriptions plus pay-as-you-go started.
Custom image specs available through the AgentBay CLI: 2c4g (default), 4c8g, 8c16g, 16c32g. The CLI's network package listing defaults to --biz-region-id cn-hangzhou. Page modified 2026-05-15.

Custom image management is a paid feature that needs a plan. This page says at most 2 custom images can be enabled at once, while the billing page says 5. An enabled image's dedicated resource pool is reclaimed after 30 days without connections. Page modified 2025-11-19.

Security whitepaper (modified 2026-10-13):
- Each sandbox is a hardware-virtualized VM with its own guest kernel and its own isolated file system, with encryption at rest and in transit.
- Sandboxes get no public IP. Sandboxes are isolated from each other by default.
- Session environments are destroyed on timeout or termination.
- The domain allow/deny policy (up to 300 rules) 'currently only supports Windows sandboxes'. *.aliyun.com, *.aliyuncs.com, *.alicdn.com, *.gws.aliyun, *.aliyunpds.com and *.aliyuncds.com are always allowed.
- Customers are responsible for outbound network policy and for protecting temporary links (desktop URLs, getLink).
- Using sandboxes with fake accounts for 刷单/刷榜 (order-brushing and ranking manipulation) is prohibited.
- The certifications listed (ISO 27001, SOC, 等保 and others) are Alibaba Cloud-wide, not AgentBay-specific.

The FAQ (modified 2025-08-18) says each user gets an isolated VM environment that is reset when the session ends and keeps no data. Cloud data is not retained 'unless the user explicitly authorizes'. User state such as cookies is kept by a self-developed persistence layer. Live streaming uses Wuying's ASP protocol.
The billing page says storage is used to persist context data and session replay records. Persisted cookies and recordings therefore live in AgentBay-managed storage.

The domestic product page claims KMS encryption 'meeting national cryptography (国密) requirements', append-only audit logs, and human confirmation checkpoints with operator takeover. It gives the concurrency claim two ways: '千级' (thousands) and '万级' (tens of thousands).
Launch: officially released at WAIC on 2025-07-31 after more than three months of internal testing, with over 1,000 beta customers.

Paper: 'AgentBay: A Hybrid Interaction Sandbox for Seamless Human-AI Intervention in Agentic Systems', submitted 2025-12-04. It claims about 5% lower end-to-end latency and up to 50% less bandwidth than RDP for its ASP streaming protocol.

The Web SDK used for embedding live view requires accepting the 无影云电脑 SDK privacy policy. It states that documents, SDK and clients are 'for use by yourself or your enterprise only' and must not be passed to third parties without Alibaba Cloud consent. Page modified 2026-09-28.

The repo already has an AgentBay note dated 2026-10-28 (section 8.8). It decided not to use AgentBay for the agent sandbox and suggests that a later cloud-browser feature could call it from the Tokyo server as a platform tool, preferring the international site in Singapore.

implications: If we buy, the minimum real cost for agent-driven Playwright/CDP control is the Pro plan, CNY 999/month or USD 149/month, plus per-second compute. The free Basic plan does not expose the CDP endpoint. An SDK-only path (BrowserOperator natural-language act/extract) may work on Basic but costs Credits and is not equivalent to a CDP connection; this is inferred from the docs and not tested.

Compute cost rough estimate, assuming a 2c4g browser session (the documented default spec for custom images; the browser_latest spec itself is not published): 2 × 0.12 + 4 × 0.05 = about CNY 0.44 per running hour domestic, or 2 × 0.027 + 4 × 0.0113 = about USD 0.10 per hour international. This is my arithmetic, not a published per-session price. Idle sessions are billed, so the agent must delete sessions promptly.

We run from a domestic-site account in Tokyo, and AgentBay documents no Tokyo region. A domestic key would put browser sessions in mainland China (Hangzhou or Shanghai). Browsing would then most likely leave from a mainland IP: no doc states the egress location directly, but sandboxes have no public IP and use regional bandwidth, so this is inferred. Overseas sites would be subject to mainland network conditions unless we add a proxy. The alternative is an international-site account and key in Singapore or Virginia, which is a separate account and bill.

AgentBay's browser features line up with our needs: CDP for the agent, cookie persistence through a Context per user, and a resource_url or Web SDK live view for human takeover inside the iOS/Android app. Persisted cookies and replays sit in Alibaba-managed storage, which is a data-handling point we would need to tell users about.

AgentBay's own outbound domain allowlist works only on Windows sandboxes, and *.aliyuncs.com is always allowed. A Linux browser sandbox therefore cannot be held to our planned egress allowlist on the AgentBay side. Instead we would rely on its SOCKS5 network redirection or a custom proxy pointing at our own egress proxy; that mapping is my inference.

Maturity risks for a production dependency:
- Several features are labelled Beta: image management, Network, ContextMount, hybrid usage.
- GetLink was whitelist-only in Oct 2025.
- Docs contradict each other: the default endpoint (Shanghai vs Hangzhou), basic bandwidth (5 vs 10 Mbps), the custom-image limit (2 vs 5) and the domestic billing example.
- The international docs contain '[To be verified in console]' placeholders.
- No product SLA was found.

Building our own browser (headless Chromium in our ACS sandbox or a separate container, driven by CDP) avoids the CNY 999/month plan floor, the region mismatch and the egress-control gap. It costs engineering effort on stealth, CAPTCHA, live view and replay. AgentBay ships those features (CAPTCHA is slider-only).
unknowns: The CPU and memory spec, and whether it can be chosen, for the browser_latest system image. No official page states it. The custom-image specs are 2c4g, 4c8g, 8c16g and 16c32g, but no doc confirms browser_latest uses one of these.

The full list of regions where sessions physically run on each site. No official region list exists. Tokyo, Japan and Hong Kong are not mentioned anywhere I found. Whether a domestic account can launch sessions in any region other than Hangzhou or Shanghai is undocumented.

The exact egress IP location and IP reputation of the default (non-proxied) browser session. No document states it. The Wuying proxy node locations and prices are not documented, and the managed proxy requires contacting sales.

Whether the CDP endpoint (get_endpoint_url / GetCdpLink) is still restricted to Pro/Ultra today, and whether GetLink is still whitelist-only. The help page dated 2026-03-16 says paid plan only. The current SDK calls a separate GetCdpLink API, and I could not test it without an account.
The validity period and allowed number of opens for resource_url / live-view links. The docs only say they are limited.
Where Playwright-initiated browser downloads land inside browser_latest, and whether files can be fetched back with file_system.download_file. This is not documented.
Whether an AgentBay product SLA exists. None was found; only Premium bandwidth is described as 'with SLA'.
Whether AgentBay has an explicit GA versus preview label. None was found. It has been commercially billed since 2025-10-28.
The year of the international pages' 'Updated: Jun 25 / Aug 28 / Jun 02' stamps. The pages do not show it.

Independent user complaints or reviews. Searches of Zhihu, V2EX, CSDN and GitHub issues found almost none. There are only about 10 closed GitHub issues, and the relevant ones are the GetLink whitelist (#407), a browser init failure (#390) and proxy configuration (#419).
Pricing pages show no browser-specific per-minute price. Only per-core-hour and per-GB-hour compute prices apply, plus the trial point rates.

maps.summary:
There are three realistic ways to give a cloud agent a browser besides AgentBay.

(A) Run Chromium ourselves inside the agent's own ACS pod. Add it to the image or run it as a sidecar container, and drive it with Playwright, playwright-mcp or agent-browser.
- The building blocks are mature and mostly Apache/MIT licensed.
- Extra cost is roughly 0.18 元/h for +1 vCPU/2 GiB in Tokyo at the ACS general-purpose default rate (0.0886 元/vCPU·h, 0.0443 元/GiB·h). In mainland China the same is 0.12 元/h (0.06 and 0.03).
- The browser profile can sit in the instance's existing persisted workspace.
- Live view can be CDP Page.startScreencast relayed through our gateway, or Xvfb + noVNC.

(B) Alibaba Cloud Function Compute "AgentRun" / the newer "FC Cloud Sandbox". It has a browser template: CDP at wss://host/ws/automation, VNC at /ws/livestream, recommended 4 vCPU/8 GiB, E2B-compatible SDK.
- Mainland prices: Eco tier 0.060 元/vCPU·h and 0.030 元/GiB·h (the same as ACS general-purpose); Std and Pro are higher.
- It is an invite-only preview, and the region list (including Tokyo) is not published.
- It is a separate sandbox from the agent's own, so profile persistence is ours to solve.
- noVNC cannot connect directly: the endpoint requires an X-Access-Token header, so a header-injecting proxy is needed.
- ACS also has its own "Agent Sandbox" compute: 0.078/0.039 元 mainland, 0.1232/0.0616 元 overseas, with hibernation and E2B compatibility.
- Wuying cloud desktops (无影云电脑) are human VDI, priced by package or hourly, and a poor fit for per-agent automation.

(C) International SaaS, useful as price and feature references. Browser-hour prices: Browserbase $0.10–0.12, Steel $0.08–0.10, Hyperbrowser $0.10, Anchor about $0.09, Browserless 30-second units that work out to about $0.18–0.24/h. Residential proxy traffic costs $8–12/GB on top. All are US/EU-hosted; Browserbase offers APAC only on enterprise request, and Steel lists only US regions. Sending Chinese users' cookies and logins abroad brings in PIPL Articles 38/39.

The decisive practical issue is where the browser's traffic leaves (its egress IP), not the browser engine:
- Since the 2022 rules, Chinese platforms show the IP location on posts; Xiaohongshu shows the country for overseas IPs, so a Tokyo browser posts as "日本".
- Taobao and WeChat web restrict overseas or new-device logins. The evidence here is anecdotal; official policy is not published.
- Datacenter IPs are a primary bot signal.
- Mainland IPs cannot reach Google, YouTube, Wikipedia, X, ChatGPT and others. Self-built cross-border tunnels need licensed channels (MIIT 2017 notice).
- Mainland hosting needs an ICP filing for any domain pointing at the servers. Automated collection must follow Article 18 of the Network Data Security Regulations (in force 2025-01-01).

Likely best mix: a self-built browser in the agent's own sandbox for general and foreign sites; a mainland-region browser pool (or AgentRun mainland) only if Chinese sites matter; and the user's own computer, via the existing desktop/relay computer tools, for login-heavy Chinese sites (banks, Taobao, WeChat). The user's computer has the right IP, device and cookies.

Licenses to avoid in our service:
- Browserless: SSPL-1.0 or commercial; SSPL §13 would force releasing our whole service stack.
- AGPL tools: nodriver, Lightpanda.

Repo notes:
- deploy/templates/Dockerfile currently has no Chromium, Xvfb or VNC.
- The Claude template is 1 vCPU/2 GiB (docs/sandbox-acs.md:28), so a browser needs more headroom.
- For WBS 14.4 (desktop chromiumoxide): Chrome 136+ ignores --remote-debugging-port on the default profile, so we cannot drive the user's everyday Chrome profile over CDP.

facts.claim: FC browser template: you first build a named template from the image fc-e2b-registry.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com/runtime/browser:v0.0.44. CDP is at wss://<sandbox-host>/ws/automation and works with Puppeteer and Playwright. VNC is at wss://<sandbox-host>/ws/livestream. Default service port is 3000. Recommended/default spec is 4 vCPU, 8192 MB RAM, 10 GB disk. Every endpoint needs an X-Access-Token header; noVNC from a plain browser cannot send it and gets 403 on direct connection. Page last updated Sep 16, 2026.
The Chinese browser-template page gives the same endpoints. For other regions you replace the region in the image address; it lists no E2B_DOMAIN values and no region list.

FC Cloud Sandbox replaces AgentRun Sandbox. It is described as nearly 100% compatible with the E2B SDK and adds Pause/Resume, snapshots, Docker-in-Docker, get_host(port), light/deep sleep and 1:N fork. Official templates include Code Interpreter, Browser and AIO. The page claims a 50–70% total cost reduction (2C4G example). Storage list price falls from ¥0.0198 to ¥0.0021 per GB-hour. No regions are listed; the console link uses cn-beijing.

FC Agent Sandbox mainland prices (invite-only beta), in 元 per hour: Eco 0.060/vCPU and 0.030/GiB; Std 0.078 and 0.039; Pro 0.120 and 0.060. Disk is 0.0021 元/GiB·h (overseas 0.001672) with 15 GiB free per sandbox. Billed per second, invoiced hourly. Light hibernation (Pro only) bills memory and disk only; deep hibernation bills disk at memory×2 + disk. Overseas availability depends on the invite agreement or an official announcement.

The international FC Agent Sandbox page gives USD rates: Eco $0.00936/vCPU·h and $0.004608/GiB·h; Std $0.01224 and $0.006012; Pro $0.01872 and $0.00936. It is labelled an invite-only preview. Updated Aug 20, 2026.

The AgentRun overview says the browser sandbox supports CDP over WebSocket with Puppeteer and Playwright, and that All-in-One is planned. It names no regions; the console link uses ap-southeast-1. Updated Aug 22, 2026.
An Alibaba developer article (2025-12-19) says the AgentRun Browser Sandbox has a built-in headless browser, a VNC client and operation recording. Its example uses a 1800 s idle timeout.
FC sandbox functions are available only in some regions; Hangzhou is the example. Session lifetime is 60–86400 s, and session concurrency is fixed at 1.

ACS pay-as-you-go prices in CNY. General-purpose default: mainland 0.06 元/vCPU·h and 0.03 元/GiB·h; Hong Kong and overseas (which covers Tokyo) 0.0886 and 0.0443. General-purpose best-effort: mainland 0.012 and 0.006; overseas 0.0177 and 0.0089. Ephemeral storage is 0.0021 (mainland) or 0.001672 (overseas) 元/GiB·h, with 30 GiB free while running but none while dormant.
The same ACS rates in USD on the international page: mainland general-purpose default $0.00936/vCPU·h and $0.0046/GiB·h; HK/overseas $0.013716 and $0.0069. Page updated Oct 09, 2026.

ACS Agent Sandbox uses MicroVM isolation, has an E2B-compatible SDK and lists Browser Use among its scenarios. Hibernation keeps memory and restores in about 1–10 s, with no CPU or memory charge while hibernated. Prices: mainland 0.078 元/vCPU·h and 0.039 元/GiB·h; HK/overseas 0.1232 and 0.0616. Tokyo is not named.
ACS Agent Sandbox (default compute quality) price cut effective 2026-06-15 12:00 Beijing time. General-purpose and performance prices are unchanged.
ACS pods get a 64 MiB /dev/shm by default. It can be enlarged by mounting an emptyDir with medium: Memory and a sizeLimit (the example uses 256 MiB).

Playwright's Docker docs recommend --ipc=host, without which Chromium can run out of memory and crash, plus --init. Running as root disables the Chromium sandbox; for untrusted sites, use a separate user and a seccomp profile. Image is mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble.
Measured Playwright Chromium peak memory idling on example.com: headed 1094 MB, headless 706 MB, minimal-flags headless 690 MB. Real sites need more; no CPU figures are given.
In Chrome's new headless mode (since 112), headless runs the same code as regular Chrome. Since Chrome 132 the old implementation ships only as the separate chrome-headless-shell binary.

CDP Page.startScreencast, screencastFrame and screencastFrameAck are marked experimental. Parameters: format, quality, maxWidth, maxHeight, everyNthFrame, maxFramesInFlight, sendLastFrame. Input.dispatchMouseEvent and dispatchKeyEvent are stable; Input.insertText (for IME) is experimental.

Microsoft playwright-mcp: Apache-2.0, about 38.8k stars, uses the accessibility tree rather than screenshots. Flags include --cdp-endpoint, --user-data-dir, --isolated, --storage-state, --headless, --proxy-server and --allowed/--blocked-origins (documented as not a security boundary). The Docker image is headless Chromium only. Latest npm @playwright/mcp is 0.0.83 (2026-09-28), still pre-1.0.

Google chrome-devtools-mcp: Apache-2.0, about 54.4k stars, built on Puppeteer, supports performance traces, network and console. Usage statistics are ON by default (disable with --no-usage-statistics), and it may send trace URLs to the CrUX API. Officially supports Chrome and Chrome for Testing only. Latest npm 1.12.0 (2026-10-22).

vercel-labs agent-browser: Apache-2.0, about 44.8k stars, a native Rust CLI. It offers accessibility snapshots with element refs, --cdp connect, --profile for persistent profiles, --session --restore to save cookies and localStorage, --headed mode, and WebSocket streaming of JPEG frames for live view. Latest npm 0.41.0 (2026-10-29); first published 2026-01-11, so it is young.

browser-use: MIT, about 119.4k stars, Python. It can control a remote browser over CDP. Stealth, residential proxies, CAPTCHA solving and live view are features of its paid cloud, which advertises 'from $0.02/hour'. Latest PyPI 0.13.14 (2026-10-26), pre-1.0.
Playwright library: Apache-2.0, latest npm 1.64.1.

steel-browser (open source): Apache-2.0, about 7.9k stars. Provides a sessions API, CDP via Puppeteer/Playwright/Selenium, stealth plugins and fingerprint management, proxy chains, extensions, and cookie/localStorage state across requests. Runs as docker ghcr.io/steel-dev/steel-browser (ports 3000/9223). The project describes itself as 'in public beta'.
Browserless: about 13.9k stars, licensed 'SSPL-1.0 OR Browserless Commercial License'. Closed-source commercial use needs a commercial license. Image is ghcr.io/browserless/chromium.

SSPL §13: anyone who makes the program's functionality available to third parties as a service must publish the 'Service Source Code', meaning all programs used to provide the service, including management, UI, APIs, automation, monitoring, backup, storage and hosting software.

Licenses of live-view and anti-bot components: noVNC core is MPL-2.0; KasmVNC and TigerVNC are GPL-2.0; X.Org server (Xvfb) uses MIT-style licenses; neko (WebRTC remote browser) is Apache-2.0; Camoufox is MPL-2.0; patchright is Apache-2.0; puppeteer-extra is MIT; nodriver and Lightpanda are AGPL-3.0.

agent-infra/sandbox ('AIO Sandbox'): Apache-2.0, about 6.2k stars. One container bundles browser (VNC and CDP), terminal, files, VS Code, Jupyter and MCP on port 8080. There is a mainland mirror on Volcengine (enterprise-public-cn-beijing.cr.volces.com/vefaas-public/all-in-one-sandbox:1.11.0). The K8s example uses 1 CPU/2Gi, and the Compose example uses shm_size 2gb and seccomp=unconfined.
OpenSandbox (Alibaba-linked): Apache-2.0, about 16.2k stars, a sandbox runtime for Docker and Kubernetes, with Playwright, Chrome and desktop examples.

patchright patches the Playwright CDP leaks Runtime.enable and Console.enable and removes --enable-automation. It claims to pass Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, Kasada and others; the example uses channel=chrome, headless=False and a persistent context.

Browserless docs: IP reputation and browser fingerprinting are the two primary bot-detection factors. Datacenter proxies are 'more easily detected'; high-reputation residential IPs plus a human-like fingerprint work best.

Playwright launchPersistentContext: the browser cannot be launched more than once against the same user data directory, and automating the default Chrome user profile is not supported because of Chrome policy changes.

From Chrome 136, --remote-debugging-port and --remote-debugging-pipe are ignored for the default data directory and require a non-default --user-data-dir. Google made the change because attackers were using remote debugging to steal cookies.

Browserbase plans: Free (1 browser-hour, 3 concurrent); Developer $20/mo (100 h, then $0.12/h, 1 GB proxy then $12/GB); Startup $99/mo (500 h, then $0.10/h, 5 GB then $10/GB); Scale is custom. Paid plans include CAPTCHA solving. Regions are US East, US West, EU Central and UK, with Asia Pacific on request for enterprise.
Browserbase Live View: debuggerFullscreenUrl can be embedded in an iframe, read/write or read-only. Mobile keyboards are not officially supported.
Browserbase built-in residential proxies list China (CN) among 200+ countries, but geolocation is best effort. Banking, government and webmail sites may be unreliable through them.

Steel cloud: Launch plan $0 + usage at $0.10/browser-hour; Scale $250/mo at $0.08/h. Proxy $10 or $6 per GB, CAPTCHA $3 or $1 per 1k. Max session length 15 min (Launch), 1 h (Scale), 24 h (Enterprise).
Steel cloud regions are Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington DC only. A debugUrl provides an embeddable live view.
Hyperbrowser: $0.10/browser-hour and $10/GB proxy. Plans are Free, Startup $30 and Scale $100; paid plans include automatic CAPTCHA solving.

Anchor Browser: the pricing calculator shows browser time at $0.09/hour and proxy at $8/GB. Starter is $50/mo with CAPTCHA bypass; custom regions (EU, Asia, Australia) are enterprise only; China is not mentioned.
Browserless cloud bills in 'units' of up to 30 s of browser time each. Overage is $0.0015–0.002 per unit, about $0.18–0.24/h. Regions are San Francisco, London and Amsterdam.

Wuying cloud desktop (Enterprise edition) is sold as 120 h or 250 h monthly packages, unlimited monthly, or pay-as-you-go. Illustrative price: 4 vCPU/8 GiB at $0.148/h pay-as-you-go. It includes 5 Mbps shared bandwidth, and storage is billed even while the desktop is off.
Alibaba Cloud EIP pay-by-traffic: Beijing and Hangzhou 0.80 元/GB; Tokyo 0.60 元/GB on BGP multi-line, or 3.0 元/GB on BGP 精品 (premium).
BGP (multi-ISP) Pro EIPs avoid the detour through international carriers between overseas regions and mainland China. Pay-as-you-go availability includes Japan (Tokyo).
互联网用户账号信息管理规定 Article 12 requires platforms to show account IP-location information (in force 2022-08-01).
From April 2022, Xiaohongshu shows IP location on profiles: province for domestic IPs, country or region for overseas IPs. Weibo and Douyin did the same.
Anecdotal (forum) reports describe overseas-IP Taobao accounts being kicked offline or restricted, and frequent page opens triggering slider CAPTCHAs. No official Taobao policy was found.

WeChat web login: since about 2017, new accounts get 'for your account security, newly registered WeChat accounts cannot log in to web WeChat'. Later reports say web WeChat is unsupported for many accounts. No current official rule was found.
Blocked in mainland China: Google (fully since 2014), YouTube, Wikipedia (since 2019), X, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit and ChatGPT. GitHub is partially blocked. Page last edited 2026-10-22.

MIIT 2017 notice (信管函〔2017〕32号): building or renting dedicated lines or VPNs for cross-border business without approval is prohibited. Companies may rent cross-border lines from licensed carriers for their own use.
Alibaba Cloud's service terms forbid using its services as an illegal proxy server. Azure China's rectification notice says no one may host illegal 翻墙 (circumvention) proxies or VPNs.

Article 18 of the 网络数据安全管理条例 (Network Data Security Regulations): processors using automated tools to access or collect network data must assess the impact on the network service, must not illegally intrude into others' networks, and must not disrupt normal operation of the service. In force 2025-01-01.

ICP filing: any domain resolving to a mainland server needs filing, on any port and even for API-only use. HK and overseas servers need no filing. Paid services may also apply for a 经营性 ICP license (commercial ICP licence).

PIPL Article 38 requires a CAC security assessment, certification or the CAC standard contract before sending personal information abroad. Article 39 requires informing the individual and obtaining separate consent.
facts.source: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/中华人民共和国个人信息保护法

facts.claim: Repo context: deploy/templates/Dockerfile has no Chromium, Xvfb or VNC. The Claude template runs at 1 vCPU/2 GiB. A paused ACS sandbox is billed for 30 GiB of temporary storage, about ¥36/month. Desktop browser control via chromiumoxide is WBS 14.4 (P3).

implications:
Self-built inside the existing sandbox is the cheapest and simplest option. Install Chromium plus Playwright, playwright-mcp or agent-browser in the agent image, or run it as a second container in the same ACS pod.
- Marginal cost at the general-purpose default rate: +1C2G is about 0.177 元/h in Tokyo or 0.12 元/h in mainland; +2C4G is about 0.354 元/h in Tokyo or 0.24 元/h in mainland.
- That is several times below the SaaS browser-hour prices of $0.08–0.12, and it adds no new vendor.
- The browser profile lives in the already-persisted workspace, so logins survive.
- Use one profile per instance and never share it: a profile directory cannot be opened twice.
- Enlarge /dev/shm with a memory-backed emptyDir.
- Raise pod memory beyond today's 1 vCPU/2 GiB Claude template; idle headless Chromium alone peaks around 700 MB.

Live view for the phone app does not need VNC. Run CDP Page.startScreencast (JPEG frames) in the sandbox, relay it over our existing gateway WebSocket, and send taps and keys back with Input.dispatchMouseEvent/dispatchKeyEvent. For Chinese IME text, use the experimental Input.insertText.
- The screencast methods are marked experimental, so pin the Chromium version.
- Use Xvfb + noVNC (MPL-2.0) or neko (Apache-2.0, WebRTC) only if a headful browser is needed for anti-bot reasons or for a full-desktop view.

FC AgentRun / Cloud Sandbox has the right feature shape: CDP, VNC, recording, an E2B SDK, hibernation and fork.
- Its unit price equals ACS general-purpose (Eco) or ACS Agent Sandbox (Std), so it is not cheaper per vCPU.
- It adds a second sandbox per agent and leaves profile persistence for us to solve.
- It is an invite-only preview with unpublished regions, and its VNC requires a header-injecting proxy.
- Treat it as a candidate for a mainland browser pool, not a replacement for the agent's own browser.

ACS Agent Sandbox (MicroVM isolation, E2B-compatible, hibernation without CPU or memory billing) already sits in our ACS clusters. It may be the lowest-friction managed option for Tokyo, but whether Tokyo offers it must be checked (the docs say only 'overseas').

Egress location is the real product decision.
- Tokyo IPs work for foreign sites. On Xiaohongshu, Weibo or Douyin they label the user's posts with a 日本 (Japan) IP location, and they likely trigger Taobao, WeChat and bank risk controls.
- Mainland IPs work for Chinese sites but cannot reach Google, GitHub (partly), ChatGPT and others, and we cannot legally tunnel around that.
- Likely architecture: a per-instance browser in Tokyo by default; an optional mainland-region browser pool for Chinese-site tasks, which needs a mainland ACS or FC deployment and ICP filing for any domain pointing at it; and the user's own computer via the paired desktop app for logged-in Chinese sites (bank, Taobao, WeChat), since it has the real IP, device and cookies.
If we serve Chinese sites from Tokyo, use the BGP 精品 EIP line (3.0 元/GB, against 0.6 元/GB for standard BGP) for latency. This does not change the IP-location label or risk-control behaviour.

Anti-bot work is an arms race we should not promise to win. Datacenter IPs are the first signal. Residential proxies from SaaS cost $8–12/GB, and buying mainland residential IPs raises its own compliance questions. Prefer headful or new-headless Chrome plus a persistent real profile. Patchright (Apache-2.0) fixes the known Playwright CDP leaks. Do not market CAPTCHA bypassing; Article 18 of the Network Data Security Regulations frames automated collection as impact-assessed and non-disruptive.

Licensing rules for a hosted service:
- Safe: Playwright, playwright-mcp, chrome-devtools-mcp, agent-browser, steel-browser and patchright (Apache-2.0); browser-use and puppeteer-extra (MIT); noVNC (MPL-2.0); Xvfb (MIT-style).
- Fine server-side unless distributed: KasmVNC and TigerVNC (GPL-2.0).
- Avoid: Browserless open source (SSPL §13 would force publishing our whole stack); nodriver and Lightpanda (AGPL-3.0, network-use copyleft).
- chrome-devtools-mcp sends usage statistics by default, and its performance tools can send page URLs to Google CrUX. Disable both, or our users' browsing URLs leak.

International SaaS (Browserbase, Steel, Hyperbrowser, Anchor, Browserless) is US/EU-hosted. Using it means users' cookies and session data leave China, which needs PIPL Article 38/39 measures (standard contract plus separate consent). Their live view and proxy features are a good feature checklist. They are not a fit as the main browser for mainland users. Note that our Tokyo deployment already raises the same cross-border question for workspace data.

WBS 14.4 (desktop app via chromiumoxide): Chrome 136+ will not expose CDP on the user's default profile. Options are a dedicated automation profile the user logs into once (simplest), a browser extension, or Chrome for Testing. Plan this before promising 'use my logged-in browser'.
Wuying cloud desktops are sold as human VDI with monthly packages and 5 Mbps shared bandwidth. They are not a sensible per-agent browser substrate compared with ACS pods or FC/ACS agent sandboxes.
unknowns: The FC Cloud Sandbox / AgentRun region list, including whether Tokyo (ap-northeast-1) is offered. Docs mention mainland, Singapore and Hong Kong image addresses and a cn-beijing console link but give no list. It is also unclear whether the browser template needs invite activation and when it goes GA.
Whether ACS Agent Sandbox is available in Tokyo. Docs only say 'Hong Kong and overseas'.
The exact semantics of ACS best-effort compute quality (whether and how pods can be preempted). Not re-verified here, so do not plan a browser on best-effort until it is checked.

Maximum /dev/shm sizeLimit on ACS pods, and whether ACS allows the seccomp or user-namespace settings Chromium's own sandbox needs. Running with --no-sandbox inside a MicroVM pod may be acceptable but is unverified.

Real Chromium CPU and memory needs for target sites (Taobao, Xiaohongshu, heavy SPAs). Only an idle example.com measurement was found (about 700 MB headless, about 1.1 GB headed). The FC template recommends 4 vCPU/8 GiB without justification.

Official Taobao, Xiaohongshu, WeChat and bank policies on overseas-IP or datacenter-IP logins and automated access. Only anecdotal forum reports were found. Bank web portals' plugin or U-shield requirements from a Linux cloud browser were not verified.
Whether Browserbase, Steel, Hyperbrowser, Anchor and Browserless endpoints are reachable and usable with acceptable latency from mainland China, and how good their CN residential proxies are.

The full text and usage restrictions of Alibaba Cloud CEN cross-border (China Unicom) agreements, for example whether a mainland browser pool could legally use them to reach foreign sites on behalf of end users. Assume not without legal advice.

Whether operating a paid agent service with automated browsing in mainland regions needs a 经营性 ICP licence or other value-added telecom licence beyond ICP filing, plus generative-AI filing. Legal advice is needed; only the filing requirement is confirmed.
Wuying cloud desktop availability and pricing in Tokyo, and whether it offers an API suitable for per-agent automation.
Exact GitHub star counts and release dates were read from GitHub pages via WebFetch (the API was blocked) and may be approximate.

maps.summary:
Only two of our five agents have a built-in browser tool: OpenClaw (its `browser` tool, driving a managed Chromium through playwright-core) and Hermes 0.19.0 (browser_navigate and related tools, driving the npm `agent-browser` CLI). Both can attach to an existing Chromium through a CDP URL. Claude Code, Codex and Pi have no browser of their own that works in our sandbox. Claude in Chrome needs the extension in a real local Chrome plus a claude.ai login, and it is turned off when Claude Code authenticates with an API key or token, which ours does through the gateway. Codex's "Browser" exists only in the ChatGPT desktop app ("isn't available in Codex CLI"). Pi's default tools are read/bash/edit/write. All five agents can use an MCP browser server, either Playwright MCP (`--cdp-endpoint`, `--executable-path`, `--headless`, `--no-sandbox`, `--proxy-server`) or chrome-devtools-mcp (`--browserUrl`/`--wsEndpoint`). Claude, Codex and Hermes take it per session through ACP. OpenClaw and Pi ignore or reject per-session MCP, so we would have to write it into their own config files (openclaw.json `mcp.servers`, `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`). That same gap means our platform tools, computer_* included, do not reach OpenClaw or Pi today.

Today none of the agents can browse in our sandbox. The image has no Chromium, no agent-browser and no CJK fonts. More importantly, ACS and Cube sandboxes have internet access turned off and allow outbound traffic only to the model gateway, and the planned egress gateway (WBS 2.7) is not built yet.

Recommended uniform design:
1. Bake one headless Chromium into the image (Debian trixie `chromium` or `chromium-headless-shell`, plus fonts-noto-cjk).
2. Have agent-shim start it as a sidecar listening on 127.0.0.1 only, with `--proxy-server` pointing at a policy-enforcing egress proxy.
3. Expose it to every agent through one MCP browser server (Playwright MCP attached via `--cdp-endpoint`), injected the same way as platform tools. Per-session for Claude, Codex and Hermes. Through config.rs-rendered files for OpenClaw and Pi.
4. Either turn off OpenClaw's and Hermes's native browser tools, or point them at the same Chromium (OpenClaw `browser.profiles.<name>.cdpUrl` + `attachOnly`; Hermes `BROWSER_CDP_URL`, which also requires installing agent-browser).

An external CDP service on loopback also needs attachOnly: true, and URLs may carry ?token= or basic auth. Complete egress isolation requires owner-side isolation or a policy-enforcing proxy.'

The `user`/existing-session profile (Chrome DevTools MCP) and the extension driver attach to a real signed-in Chrome on the user's own machine.

implications: Answer to 'which agents can browse natively': only OpenClaw and Hermes, and neither works in our sandbox yet (no Chromium, no agent-browser, no internet). Claude, Codex and Pi need an MCP browser server. Vendor browser features (Claude in Chrome, Codex Browser and Chrome extension) are ruled out: they need the user's local browser extension, the vendor desktop app, or the vendor's own login.

Uniform design: (1) install Chromium (Debian `chromium` or `chromium-headless-shell`) and fonts-noto-cjk in deploy/templates/Dockerfile. This adds about 230-324 MB per image, so add a manifest or template flag rather than putting it in every image unconditionally. (2) Have agent-shim start it as a sidecar: `--headless --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=~/.browser --proxy-server=<egress proxy>`, plus `--no-sandbox` if user namespaces are unavailable. (3) Inject one MCP browser server, e.g. `npx`-free pinned `@playwright/mcp --cdp-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9222`, into all five agents.

Injecting the MCP server: per-session ACP mcpServers already works for Claude, Codex and Hermes. For OpenClaw, config.rs must write `mcp.servers` into openclaw.json. For Pi, it must write ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json with `exposure: "direct"`. That same change also delivers schedule_*, artifact_* and computer_* to OpenClaw and Pi, which currently get none of them (shim.rs:67-72), so it is worth doing on its own merits.

Native tools: either turn them off to keep one browser surface and one policy (OpenClaw plugins.entries.browser.enabled=false or browser.enabled=false; Hermes: drop the browser tools from the toolset), or point them at the same Chromium. For OpenClaw that means browser.defaultProfile set to a profile with cdpUrl http://127.0.0.1:9222 and attachOnly true. For Hermes it means BROWSER_CDP_URL plus an `agent-browser` npm install in the image, because without it Hermes advertises the tools and then fails trying to `npx agent-browser`.

Platform tool or native tool: an in-sandbox browser should be an agent-side MCP tool that runs inside the sandbox, next to the agent, not an orchestrator platform tool. computer_* goes through the orchestrator and relay because its target is the user's device and needs phone approval. Sending every browser snapshot and screenshot through the orchestrator would add latency and load for no isolation gain. The orchestrator-platform-tool route fits only a remote cloud browser (AgentBay, AgentRun browser sandbox, Browserbase) whose credentials and egress stay on the server side.

Build vs buy: build first. Chromium, Playwright MCP and agent-browser are open source, so the only cost is sandbox CPU and RAM, and the design keeps the existing one-sandbox-per-instance isolation. AgentBay would add stealth, captcha solving and residential proxies, but on our domestic account it runs only in mainland China. Its CDP URL would also have to be added to the sandbox allowOut list or proxied, and its CDP endpoint fits the same `--cdp-endpoint` slot, so it can be added later without changing what the agents see.

Hard prerequisite: the egress proxy (WBS 2.7). Without it a sandbox browser can only reach localhost, for example dev servers the agent starts. Browser-level allowlists (Playwright --allowed-origins, OpenClaw ssrfPolicy, Hermes url_safety) are explicitly not security boundaries. Enforce policy, including blocking 100.100.100.200 and private ranges, in the proxy, and pass it to Chromium with --proxy-server.

Sizing: Codex and Pi run in 1 GB. A headless Chromium alongside the agent will likely need those raised to 2 GB when browsing is on; this is an estimate to measure in the ACS test. Persisting the browser profile under the state dir keeps site logins across wakes, but cookies then sit in OSS workspace archives, which affects the privacy policy.

For sites where the user is already logged in on their own machine, the right path is the existing computer_* / desktop app plan (WBS 14.4 chromiumoxide). It plays the role Claude in Chrome plays, without depending on a vendor extension.
The license scan (tools/licenses policy) will need entries for the Chromium Debian package and any added npm packages (@playwright/mcp, playwright-core, agent-browser).

options.name: SELF-BUILT: headless Chromium inside each agent's own sandbox, driven over CDP (Playwright MCP), egress through our own proxy, live view and takeover via CDP screencast over the existing envd exec path. Variants: (a) a browser sidecar container in the same pod, (b) an on-demand separate browser pod per instance.
options.architecture:
Notation: [A#] is an assumption, defined in cost_model. "(unverified)" means nobody has tested it on ACS yet. BASE DESIGN: the browser runs in the agent's own container. 1) Template image. deploy/templates/Dockerfile gets an optional browser layer, switched on by a new [browser] section in the manifest (crates/catalog/src/manifest.rs and manifests/*.toml). The layer contains: - Debian trixie `chromium` 156: 89.6 MB download, 324 MB installed. - `fonts-noto-cjk`: 55.3 MB download, 91.2 MB installed (verified on packages.debian.org today; without it Chinese pages render as boxes). - a pinned `@playwright/mcp@0.0.83`. Expected growth is about 0.45–0.6 GB per template, on top of today's 0.5–0.9 GB [A9]. Browser-enabled templates also need a bigger spec: at least 1 vCPU / 4 GiB, 2 vCPU / 4 GiB recommended [A5]. On ACS, CPU and memory are set per SandboxSet (docs/sandbox-acs.md:28), so each browser variant gets its own SandboxSet in deploy/aliyun/acs.py. The ACS general-purpose spec table allows 1 vCPU with 1–8 GiB and 2 vCPU with 2–16 GiB in 1 GiB steps (help.aliyun.com/zh/cs/user-guide/acs-pod-instance-overview, verified). Whether the agent-sandbox compute class uses the same table is not documented. 2) Browser process. agent-shim supervises Chromium as a sidecar, using the same mechanism as OpenClaw's gateway: crates/agent-shim/src/shim.rs start_sidecars plus process::wait_tcp_ready. Chromium starts on the first browser call. Flags: - `--headless=new` - `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --remote-debugging-port=9222` - `--user-data-dir=/sandbox/workspace/.thinktin/browser/profile` - `--disk-cache-dir=/tmp/chromium-cache` (keeps the cache out of the archive) - `--proxy-server=http://:3128` - `--disable-dev-shm-usage` (ACS gives a 64 MiB /dev/shm by default) - `--disable-background-networking` (no Google update or Safe Browsing calls) - `--force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp` - `--lang=zh-CN`, a fixed 1280x800 window - `--no-sandbox` if Chromium's own sandbox cannot start as uid 1001. ACS rejects privileged pods and privilege escalation; user-namespace support is unverified. The shim restarts Chromium if it crashes. It stops Chromium after N idle minutes and when a run ends, so cookies are flushed to disk before pause or archive. It deletes stale Singleton* lock files before launch. 3) How agents drive the browser. There is one MCP server: Playwright MCP, attached with `--cdp-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9222 --no-webmcp`. It is injected the same way as the platform-tools bridge: - Claude (ACP and CLI), Codex and Hermes: per-session mcpServers (crates/agent-shim/src/main.rs:455, acp.rs:87, claude_cli.rs:111). - OpenClaw: crates/agent-shim/src/config.rs writes openclaw.json, either `mcp.servers` or the native `browser.profiles.

.cdpUrl` with attachOnly=true, so OpenClaw does not start a second Chromium. - Pi: config.rs writes ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json with exposure "direct". This is unverified under `pi --mode rpc` with PI_OFFLINE=1. - Hermes's native browser stays hidden, because agent-browser is not installed. Browser actions are NOT orchestrator platform tools. That route would add a server round trip per click, reach only 3 of the 5 agents, and trigger an approval prompt on every call. Only two small platform tools go in crates/orchestrator/src/browser.rs, because they need the server or the app: `browser_handoff` (ask the user to take over) and `browser_share` (save the current frame as an artifact the user can see). 4) Approvals. Today the shim runs with `--on-unlisted ask` (crates/orchestrator/src/exec.rs:121-127), and MCP calls do not map to a pre-authorizable ACP kind, so every click would ask the user. Two changes fix this: - Add tool-name pre-authorization, e.g. a "可以用浏览器上网" (may browse the web) scope, in crates/agent-shim/src/policy.rs and PlanPolicy. - For Claude, also write `permissions.allow: mcp__browser__*` into its settings.json when that scope is granted. 5) Egress. This is the prerequisite (WBS 2.7, not built). A new Rust forward proxy, crates/egress (`thinktin-egress`), runs on the service machine on port 3128. ACS allowOut already lets sandboxes reach the service machine's IP on every port (docs/sandbox-acs.md §5), so the only network change is one security-group rule opening 3128 to the sandbox vSwitch (deploy/aliyun/network.py GATEWAY_PORTS). No NAT, and sandboxes still have no direct internet. The proxy: - identifies the instance by source Pod IP via instances.sandbox_address (crates/store/src/instances.rs:36). This works because ACS does no SNAT. Cube's node SNAT would need a token instead. - tunnels HTTPS with CONNECT without TLS interception, and forwards plain HTTP. - resolves names itself with the public-IP-only resolver from crates/llm-gw/src/ssrf.rs. That blocks RFC1918, 100.64/10, loopback, link-local and 100.100.100.200 (the metadata service). - allows ports 80 and 443 only. - enforces per-instance connection and byte caps and an optional per-plan allowlist or denylist, has a per-instance kill switch, and keeps an access log of host and bytes. Pages are fetched from the Tokyo ECS public IP. Any process in the sandbox could use the proxy, not just Chromium. That is a policy decision WBS 2.7 has to make (open web with private ranges blocked, or allowlist). 6) Saved logins. The profile lives under workspace/.thinktin/browser, so the existing archive covers it: the workspace is tar'd, encrypted with the user's DEK and stored in OSS (crates/control/src/workspace.rs EXPORT_ARGV, crates/orchestrator/src/workspaces.rs). Changes needed: - exclude Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache, Service Worker/CacheStorage and Singleton*; - cap the profile size (archives above 4 GiB are not archived); - close Chromium before tar, so the SQLite cookie database is consistent. A paused sandbox keeps the browser process frozen in memory. An archived one keeps only the profile on disk. In Tokyo, archive happens after 1 hour paused (deploy/k8s/overlays/tokyo/server.toml). 7) Live view. No new port and no raw CDP exposed to the network. The server runs `agent-shim browser view` inside the sandbox through the existing envd exec stream (SandboxProvider::exec over /kruise//49983). That helper: - attaches to the local CDP; - calls Page.startScreencast (JPEG quality about 60, max width 1280, frame-ack flow control); - writes length-prefixed frames to stdout; - reads input events from stdin: tap, drag, wheel, key, and Input.insertText for Chinese IME. On the server: - The gateway gets a new authenticated WebSocket, `GET /v1/instances/{id}/browser/live` (crates/gateway/src/routes/browser.rs). It relays frames as binary messages and input back, allows one controller at a time, and drops frames for slow clients. - A `BrowserView` trait in gateway Inner, implemented by crates/control, finds the current sandbox, runs the exec, and touches last_active_at so idle-pause does not fire while someone is watching. - Base64 inside envd's Connect JSON adds about 33% overhead. - The 600 s sandbox-gateway idle timeout is covered by envd's 30 s keepalive. The throughput of this path is unverified. VNC/Xvfb is not needed, because headless plus screencast is enough. noVNC (MPL-2.0) is only a fallback if a headed browser is ever needed for anti-bot reasons. 8) Takeover. The agent calls `browser_handoff{reason: login|captcha|payment|confirm, message}`. Then: - The call creates an approval-like wait record (crates/store/src/approvals.rs, new wait_code) and sends a push with a deep link (a new notify kind). - The agent's turn blocks inside the tool call. The sandbox stays running, as it already does for approvals (pause_waiting_approval=false). - The user opens the live view in control mode, logs in or solves the CAPTCHA, and taps 完成 (Done). The tool returns "done". - After 30 minutes the tool returns "user did not respond" [A10]. Without a handoff, the user can watch at any time. "Take control" first interrupts the agent's current turn, so two sets of inputs never fight. 9) App. iOS (ThinktinKit/ThinktinUI, SwiftUI) and Android (Compose) each get a live-view screen, a handoff card in the conversation, a per-instance browser switch, and a "clear browser data" button. All go through a new client-core BrowserLive FFI (crates/client-core, UniFFI; tokio-tungstenite is already a dependency). VARIANT (a): browser sidecar CONTAINER in the same pod. The SandboxSet pod gets a second container from one shared browser image, with the same flags. It shares the network namespace, so CDP on 127.0.0.1:9222, Playwright MCP and the live-view helper (run through envd in the agent container) work unchanged. - Gains: one browser image for all 5 agents, so Chromium security rebuilds no longer touch agent images. The agent templates stay small. Chromium gets its own memory cgroup, so a Chromium OOM does not kill the agent. - Costs: the profile has to sit on an emptyDir shared by both containers and mounted under the workspace, or the archive misses it. Multi-container pods, emptyDir and pause/resume under the ACS agent-sandbox class are all unverified. The shim cannot supervise a process in another container. Cube templates are single-image microVMs, so Local and Cube stay on the same-container design. - Same compute cost, since ACS bills the sum of container limits. No real security gain: whoever holds CDP can read every cookie. VARIANT (b): ON-DEMAND separate browser pod per instance. The control plane creates a browser pod on the first browser call and destroys it after an idle grace period. - Pod-to-pod CDP does not fit ACS networking. allowOut is fixed per IP at creation, and allowing the sandbox CIDR would open traffic between tenants. So CDP has to be relayed: agent pod → authenticated CDP relay on the service machine → envd exec into the browser pod (a stdin/stdout ↔ 127.0.0.1:9222 pipe). That adds two hops of latency and puts all screenshot traffic through the server. - The profile has to be archived separately to OSS, reusing workspace.rs. - Cold start adds seconds unless a warm pool is kept. - Gains: we pay only for browsing minutes, and the agent's workspace files are not inside the browser pod (browser_file_upload cannot read them directly).

options.cost_model:
PRICES USED
- ACS Agent Sandbox, "Hong Kong and overseas" tier: ¥0.1232 per vCPU-hour and ¥0.0616 per GiB-hour, billed per second. Paused (hibernated) pods pay no CPU or memory. Unsupported specs are rounded up to the next supported spec. Source: help.aliyun.com/zh/cs/user-guide/agent-sandbox/, verified 2026-10-29. Our SandboxSet uses compute-class agent-sandbox (deploy/aliyun/acs.py).
- Tokyo pay-by-traffic public bandwidth: ¥0.6/GB, outbound only (docs/deploy-aliyun-sg.md §8.9). Inbound is not billed: "阿里云仅对出方向流量计费，入方向不计费" (help.aliyun.com/zh/ecs/public-bandwidth, verified). Pages the browser downloads are inbound to our proxy, so they are free.
- Economy ECS ecs.e-c1m2.large (2 cores, 4 GB): ¥117.67/month (docs/deploy-aliyun-sg.md §8.9).
- Baseline sandbox today, 1 vCPU / 2 GiB: 0.1232 + 2×0.0616 = ¥0.2464/h (docs: about ¥0.25/h).

ASSUMPTIONS
- [A1] Tokyo is billed at the "HK and overseas" price. The page names no regions.
- [A2] Each daily active user (DAU) runs their agent 60 min/day (repo §8.9 uses about 1 h/day). Month = 30 days, so 30 sandbox-hours per DAU per month.
- [A3] The browser is in use 15 min/day per DAU in the light case. Heavy case: 120 agent-min and 60 browser-min per day.
- [A4] Every DAU has browsing turned on (upper bound).
- [A5] Size needed with a browser: 1 vCPU / 4 GiB minimum, 2 vCPU / 4 GiB recommended. Basis: idle headless Chromium peaks at about 700 MB (datawookie measurement); real sites need more. Not measured on ACS.
- [A6] Live view is watched 3 min/day per DAU (heavy: 10). Average 3 fps × 50 KB JPEG ≈ 150 KB/s ≈ 9 MB/min. Unmeasured.
- [A7] About 2 pages/min of active browsing × 2.5 MB/page. HTTP Archive median is about 2.3–2.9 MB (third-party summary). Outbound proxy bytes are about 5% of inbound.
- [A8] Variant (b) browser pod is 1 vCPU / 2 GiB and lives for browser minutes + 5 min idle grace.
- [A9] Image growth of 0.45–0.6 GB costs nothing directly (ACR personal edition is free). It only slows pulls.
- [A10] Handoff timeout is 30 min. The ACS traffic-proxy sidecar (0.2 vCPU / 128 MB) may round specs up by up to about 25%; this applies to every option and to variant (b) twice.

LIGHT CASE (60 agent-min, 15 browser-min, 3 live-view-min per DAU per day)

Same container, 2 vCPU / 4 GiB:
- Price: 2×0.1232 + 4×0.0616 = ¥0.4928/h, which is +¥0.2464/h over today's size.
- Extra compute: 30 h × 0.2464 = ¥7.39 per DAU per month.
- Live view: 3 min × 9 MB = 27 MB/day, 0.81 GB/month × 0.6 = ¥0.49 per DAU.
- Proxy outbound: 15 × 2 × 2.5 MB = 75 MB/day = 2.25 GB/month inbound (free). 5% outbound = 0.11 GB × 0.6 = ¥0.07 per DAU.
- 100 DAU: 739 + 49 + 7 = about ¥795/month. The proxy runs on the existing service machine.
- 1000 DAU: 7,392 + 486 + 70 + ¥118 dedicated proxy ECS = about ¥8,066/month. Peak load is about 1000 × 15 / 1440 × 4 ≈ 42 concurrent browsers at about 1 Mbps each.

Same container, 1 vCPU / 4 GiB:
- Price: ¥0.3696/h, +¥0.1232/h. Extra compute ¥3.70 per DAU.
- 100 DAU: about ¥426/month. 1000 DAU: about ¥4,370/month.

Variant (a), sidecar container: costs the same as the matching same-container size.

Variant (b), separate browser pod:
- Pod lifetime: 20 min/day = 10 h/month × ¥0.2464 = ¥2.46 per DAU.
- 100 DAU: 246 + 49 + 7 = about ¥302/month. Add ¥180 (0.2464 × 730 h) if one warm pod is kept.
- 1000 DAU: 2,464 + 486 + 70 + 118 + 180 = about ¥3,318/month.

HEAVY CASE (120 agent-min, 60 browser-min, 10 live-view-min per DAU per day)
- Same container 2 vCPU / 4 GiB: 60 h × 0.2464 = ¥14.78 per DAU. 100 DAU about ¥1,667/month; 1000 DAU about ¥16,900/month. The 1000-DAU figure includes 2 proxy machines, about ¥235, because the peak is about 167 browsers ≈ 167 Mbps.
- Same container 1 vCPU / 4 GiB: 100 DAU about ¥928/month; 1000 DAU about ¥9,500/month.
- Variant (b): 32.5 h × 0.2464 = ¥8.01 per DAU. 100 DAU about ¥990/month; 1000 DAU about ¥10,300/month.
